summary.headline: Hikal Q4 FY26 revenue INR519 cr with 20.3% EBITDA margin, but FY26 PBT negative INR79.3 cr after INR85 cr exceptional items; no FY27 guidance given.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR519 cr with EBITDA of INR105 cr (20.3% margin) and PAT of INR14.4 cr after a INR47 cr impairment at Panoli. FY26 revenue fell to INR1,713 cr with EBITDA margin of 12.9%, and PBT was negative INR79.3 cr after INR85 cr of exceptional items (new labour code and impairments); PBT before exceptionals was about INR7 cr. Pharma was weak in H1 on a US FDA warning letter at Bangalore and recovered sequentially in H2, while Crop Protection improved on volumes. Management declined to give FY27 revenue or margin guidance until Q1 FY27 results, but said FY27 would show growth.

segments.name: Pharmaceuticals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,021 cr, EBIT INR58 cr (5.7% margin). Q4 revenue INR292 cr, EBIT INR35 cr (12% margin); plants at Panoli and Bangalore running at about 80-85% utilisation. Own-product shipments from Bangalore slowed in Q4 after the FDA warning letter.

segments.name: Crop Protection
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR692 cr, EBIT INR58 cr (8.4% margin). Q4 revenue INR228 cr with 17.1% EBIT margin (INR39 cr), driven by higher volume offtake and gradual industry normalisation.

segments.name: Animal Health
segments.commentary: No revenue figure disclosed. Management reiterated a target of a INR500 cr+ business in 4-5 years (set in Sept 2025); a CDMO multinational contract has completed product validation and moved into commercial phase.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or margin guidance; management will update after Q1 FY27 results.
Management said FY27 will show growth and that FY27 margins should sustain at improved levels, with price pass-through partly offsetting raw material inflation.
FY26 was described as a transition year, with significant growth from FY27 and meaningful growth in FY28-FY30.
The FY30 plan (earlier INR3,500-4,000 cr medium-term and INR6,000 cr FY30 targets) is said to still stand but is delayed by 2-3 years; no reaffirmation of figures.
Management expects the US FDA matter to be resolved by end of this year, with an inspection expected towards year-end; the Bangalore site is not expected to receive new approvals this year.
Pharma volumes expected to improve QoQ and grow; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter because of annual maintenance shutdowns.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR149 cr for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades and CDMO capacity. Over FY23-FY26, about INR900 cr capex, of which about INR600 cr growth and INR300 cr infra, regulatory and maintenance.

Panoli multipurpose agrochemical plant (about INR300 cr investment) impaired INR47 cr and about INR250 cr being retooled for Pharma and Animal Health lines; expected on stream next financial year (FY27).
New high-potency laboratory, expanded R&D centre in Pune and pilot plant at Panoli are now operational; expanded Kilo lab in Pune planned.
Planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY28; HPAPI and ADC chemistries expected to take 3-5 years to scale.
New Panoli facility for DMF filings; Panoli approved by US FDA in May 2023 with no warning-letter issue.
demand_pricing: Pharma: H2 FY26 demand recovered over H1, with improved demand in API and CDMO; 5-6 DMF filings targeted annually vs 2-3 historically, all from Panoli; RFP activity rising.
Crop Protection: volumes improving YoY on key products; management says inventory correction is largely over but agrochemical pricing pressure persists and China has not raised agrochemical prices.

Raw materials: solvent prices (toluene, methanol, acetone, benzene) rose sharply over the last 3 months and stayed at higher levels; availability is not an issue. CDMO pass-throughs lag by about a quarter; old products face competitive pressure, so pass-through may be partial.
Animal Health: no degrowth signalled by customers on current portfolio; move towards more complex molecules with lower competition and higher margin sustainability.
Pharma loss in Q4: some own-product business was lost in Q4 per management, though the order book is intact and CDMO demand is long term.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Pharma fall short of the 10% growth guidance given in February, and is Pharma weak YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FDA-related GMP consultant advice to slow some production at Bangalore slowed shipments and price releases in Q4; no customers lost, though some business was lost in Q4 and expected to recover over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give a FY27 top-line growth figure and a path to make up three lost years?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 guidance until Q1 results because of war-related uncertainty in raw materials and logistics. Management expects growth to return in FY27 and sees FY28-FY30 as meaningful growth years; ROCE target of 18-20% is acknowledged.

qa_highlights.question: When will the US FDA issue be resolved and what is the timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes to resolve it by end of this year; CAPAs nearly complete, milestone meetings with FDA planned in the next few months, with a likely inspection toward year-end. Typical resolution time cited as 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY30 INR3,500-4,000 cr / INR6,000 cr target still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: The FY30 plan still stands but is delayed by 2-3 years; no explicit guidance given; growth expected every year, mainly from CDMO, Pharma, Animal Health and Specialty Chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 5-6 DMF filings target include Animal Health, and how is the Animal Health ramp-up tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: 5-6 DMF filings are Pharma only; Animal Health is additional. Management reaffirmed the INR500 cr+ Animal Health target in 4-5 years and declined to give FY27 revenue guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Did Hikal sell steroid or hormone products for animal health?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hikal is not into steroids or hormones currently; the older website reference was outdated.

risks_watch: US FDA warning letter at Bangalore: resolution timing (management targets end-2026) and any new approvals from Bangalore, which management does not expect this year.
Raw material cost inflation from solvent prices and geopolitical volatility, with a one-to-two-quarter lag on CDMO pass-through and limited pass-through on old competitive products.
Q4 loss of some own-product Pharma business; management says it should recover over the next two quarters.
Capacity-utilisation metric may be inflated by longer batch cycle times after post-FDA slowdown, per management.
Impairment of INR47 cr at Panoli and retooling of about INR250 cr; the new Pharma/Animal Health lines are expected in FY27 and need to deliver returns.
Multi-year growth shortfall: FY24-FY26 revenue flat to down, and the ROCE target of 18-20% is far from current levels.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term structural tailwinds and recovery, but cautious on near-term numbers: management refused FY27 guidance and repeatedly deferred specifics to Q1 results, and acknowledged missing its February Pharma growth guidance due to the FDA-related slowdown.
key_quotes: For the quarter, revenue stood at INR519 crores with EBITDA margins improving to 20.3% over the previous quarter.
We believe the industry has now largely moved beyond the worst phase of the cycle.
But I think the worst is behind us.
FY '27, I don't want to give any guidance, as I mentioned. There's a lot of uncertainty.
